target_problem: target-compatible excess-overlap at most one for a fixed opposite-phase signed-MUX first pair when non-common V113 dominator stages may contain bounded cyclic interaction
conditional_implication: if every non-common V113 dominator stage has feedback-gate number at most one, then target-compatible overlap at most minimum_overlap+1 is decidable in polynomial time by enumerating the feedback/extra shared gates and reducing each stage to at most five fixed gate-disjoint requests in a DAG
current_gap: the theorem handles the first genuinely cyclic level but does not give f(tau) poly(N) time for arbitrary feedback-gate number tau; the direct extension grows the residual DAG request dimension with tau and yields only an XP-style route
stop_rule: do not claim an arbitrary-tau FPT extension from the product-state DAG DP alone; V117 must exploit the special ordered two-route interface to beat the variable-request DAG linkage barrier or establish a matching parameterized/hardness boundary
external_validation_target: Fortune-Hopcroft-Wyllie 1980 general directed linkage hardness, Slivkins 2010 parameterized DAG edge-disjoint-path hardness, and specialist review of the signed-MUX one-feedback-stage transfer
bridge_lemmas: V113 minimum overlap equals the number of common gate dominators
an overlap budget of minimum+1 permits at most one shared non-common gate
deleting one feedback gate and the optional shared gate leaves an acyclic stage
two gate-simple routes then decompose into at most five globally gate-disjoint DAG requests
fixed-five gate-disjoint DAG requests are solvable by a product-state token DP with no gate-history set
cross-route target constraints remain local to the preceding common gate and the optional shared gate
the exact-stretch cyclic family has feedback-gate number one and Delta exactly one for every depth
